subject: English
description: Active ↔ passive voice across tenses and moods (extended set)

questions.stem: Change to passive: 'Nobody admires a coward.'

options.option_text: A coward is not admired by anybody.
A coward is admired by nobody.
Nobody is admired by a coward.
A coward has admired nobody.

questions.explanation: Negative subject 'nobody' — standard conversion: use 'is not … by anybody' or 'is not … by any' construction. Option A is the cleaner form. B is also acceptable in informal usage ('by nobody') but slightly awkward.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Active → Passive: 'The news will shock everyone.'

options.option_text: Everyone will be shocked by the news.
The news will be shocked by everyone.
Everyone shocked by the news.
The news shocks everyone.

questions.explanation: Future simple → 'will be + past participle'. Object 'everyone' becomes subject; subject 'the news' moves to 'by' agent. 'Everyone will be shocked by the news.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Active → Passive: 'They had just completed the project.'

options.option_text: The project has been completed by them.
The project had just been completed by them.
The project was being completed by them.
The project completed them.

questions.explanation: Past PERFECT active ('had + V3') → Past perfect passive ('had been + V3'). 'Just' — adverb — stays where it is. 'had just completed' → 'had just been completed'.
questions.subject: English

options.option_text: By whom was this novel written?
This novel was written by whom?
Who was written this novel?
Whom did write this novel?

questions.explanation: Interrogative with 'Who + V_past': convert to 'By whom + was/were + object + V3?' Formal passive: 'By whom was this novel written?' Colloquial: 'Who was this novel written by?' Both are valid; the formal form is generally expected in exams.
questions.subject: English

options.option_text: This secret be kept.
Let this secret be kept.
This secret is kept.
This secret should be kept.

questions.explanation: Imperative active → passive with 'Let ... be' construction. 'Keep this secret' → 'Let this secret be kept.' For prohibitions / negative imperatives: 'Don't X' → 'Let X not be + V3' or 'You are asked not to X'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Passive form of: 'They elected him captain.'

options.option_text: He was elected captain by them.
Captain elected him by them.
He is the captain.
They were elected him captain.

questions.explanation: Double-complement verbs (elect, appoint, make, crown, consider, call etc.) keep the noun complement after the passive verb. 'He was elected captain [by them].' Similarly: 'She was made chairwoman.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Active → Passive: 'They are building a new bridge.'

options.option_text: A new bridge is being built by them.
A new bridge is built by them.
A new bridge was being built.
A new bridge has been built.

questions.explanation: Present continuous active ('are building') → passive 'is/are being + V3'. 'A new bridge is being built [by them].'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: The trophy was won by the school team in the final match last year. Which is the correct active voice form?

options.option_text: The school team wins the trophy in the final match last year
The school team won the trophy in the final match last year
The school team had won the trophy in the final match last year
The school team win the trophy in the final match last year

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'was won' is simple past passive, so the active voice must also use simple past — 'won'. Option C wrongly shifts the tense to past perfect 'had won'. Options A and D use present tense 'wins/win', which contradicts the past-time marker 'last year'.

questions.stem: All employees should follow the new safety guidelines. Which of the following is the correct passive transformation?

options.option_text: The new safety guidelines should be followed by all employees
The new safety guidelines should have followed by all employees
The new safety guidelines must be followed by all employees
The new safety guidelines should be follow by all employees

questions.explanation: A is correct: modal passive follows the pattern 'modal + be + past participle' → 'should be followed'. Option B omits 'been' (correct form would be 'should have been followed'). Option C substitutes 'must' for 'should', altering the degree of obligation. Option D uses the bare infinitive 'follow' instead of the past participle 'followed'.

questions.stem: The government has announced a new welfare scheme for farmers. Which of the following is the correct passive voice form?

options.option_text: A new welfare scheme was announced by the government for farmers
A new welfare scheme has been announced by the government for farmers
A new welfare scheme had been announced by the government for farmers
A new welfare scheme is announced by the government for farmers

questions.explanation: B is correct: present perfect active ('has announced') converts to 'has been + past participle' in the passive. Option A wrongly uses simple past passive 'was announced'. Option C uses past perfect 'had been announced', changing the tense entirely. Option D uses simple present 'is announced', which erases the present perfect aspect.

questions.stem: The fire brigade was extinguishing the blaze when we arrived. Identify the correct passive voice of this sentence.

options.option_text: The blaze was being extinguished by the fire brigade when we arrived
The blaze was extinguished by the fire brigade when we arrived
The blaze had been extinguished by the fire brigade when we arrived
The blaze is being extinguished by the fire brigade when we arrived

questions.explanation: A is correct: past continuous active ('was extinguishing') → past continuous passive ('was being extinguished'). Option B uses simple past passive, losing the sense of an ongoing action at the moment of arrival. Option C shifts to past perfect. Option D uses present continuous, clashing with the past time context established by 'when we arrived'.

questions.stem: Active: 'The authorities are reviewing all pending applications this month.' Which passive transformation is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: All pending applications are being reviewed by authorities this month
All pending applications were being reviewed by authorities this month
All pending applications are being reviewed this month by the authorities
By the authorities, all pending applications are being reviewed this month

questions.explanation: B is incorrect: 'were being reviewed' shifts the tense to past continuous, but the original verb 'are reviewing' is present continuous. Options A, C, and D all preserve the correct present continuous passive 'are being reviewed' — they are valid transformations that only differ in the placement of the agent phrase.

questions.stem: 'The witness has appeared before the court three times.' Which of the following correctly represents its passive voice?

options.option_text: The court has been appeared before by the witness three times
The witness has been appearing before the court three times
Passive cannot be formed as 'appeared' here is intransitive
Before the court, the witness has been appeared three times

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Appeared' is used intransitively here — there is no direct object that can become the subject of a passive construction. Passive voice is only possible with transitive verbs. Options A and D force 'appeared' into a passive mould incorrectly. Option B merely converts the tense to present perfect continuous without forming any passive at all.

questions.stem: 'The results are expected to be declared by the board next week.' Choose the active voice equivalent that most precisely preserves the original meaning.

options.option_text: The board expects to declare the results by next week
The board is expecting that results will be declared soon
The board expects the results to have been declared next week
The board had expected to declare all the results next week

questions.explanation: A is correct: the complex passive 'are expected to be declared by the board' converts to 'the board expects to declare', preserving the simple present tense and the active infinitive structure. Option B uses present continuous and leaves the embedded verb still passive. Option C uses a perfect infinitive 'to have been declared', implying the action should already be complete — altering the meaning. Option D shifts to past perfect 'had expected', changing the tense entirely.
